sources: https://forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/getting-429-too-many-request-for-nim-cloud-api/335755 (2025-06-11 capture, 8 repeated {"status":429,"title":"Too Many Requests"} frames; NVIDIA staff reproduced the 429 on 2025-06-12)
https://forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/api-error-429-help/376113 (2026-07-08, HTTP 429 body status/title only, model GLM-5.2)

https://forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/i-got-rate-limit-error-every-time-i-use-nvidia-nim-api/373385 (2026-06-15 Hermes log: 'Error code: 429 - {'status': 429, 'title': 'Too Many Requests'}', model moonshotai/kimi-k2.6)
https://forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/nvidia-nim-faq/300317 (official FAQ: 'The rate of requests will vary per model queried and may vary based on the number of concurrent users')
notes: The ONLY 429 body with a capture history: RFC-7807-style but with just status+title, no detail, no type, no counter name, no number. Nothing in the body says minute vs hour vs day, so window=unknown and it must NOT be read as per_day (vocabulary section 2). No Retry-After or x-ratelimit-* header is evidenced anywhere (no capture lists headers; an unauthenticated GET of /v1/models by this reviewer on 2026-10-16 returned only content-type and vary); headers=null means not evidenced, not proven absent. Scope: official FAQ says per model + concurrency; the account UI shows a per-account request rate (default ~40 RPM, community). Community cases show one model locked while others on the same account work (GLM-5.2/Kimi K3 429 while DeepSeek Flash, Nemotron, MiniMax were fine: 376113 posts 25-27, 381764 post 4), so scope=model by R18; but sibling keys of the SAME account share the lock (a user's second account worked 'for ten requests' then locked too, 376113 post 12) so rotation only helps across different accounts (R08). A third-party page claims the 40 RPM is shared across all models on a key (news.creeta.com, community, no NVIDIA source); that disagrees with the FAQ and is recorded in README as an open conflict. Same wire is used for 'low volume' 429s (1-4 requests, 373385, 381764, 371407) so the body cannot separate a true RPM breach from a capacity or abuse lock. Without any stated number: 20s unsized throttle (R23) and never multiply on repetition (R10/R11).

sources: https://forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/getting-429-too-many-request-for-nim-cloud-api/335755 (2026-06-12 post 20: '429 status code (no body) just tested again at now and still 429')
notes: A single user report of a 429 with an empty body during a multi-hour lock. Whether this is the gateway dropping the JSON, the client discarding it, or a genuinely distinct shape is not established; treat it as the same decision as the problem+json 429. A 429 with an empty body must not fall through to the host's blind hour (R23). headers=null: not evidenced.

message_template: {status:429,title:Too Many Requests} (same wire as the short 429)
sources: https://forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/getting-429-too-many-request-for-nim-cloud-api/335755 (2026-06-12: GLM-5.1 still 429 after >2 h; others ~3 h)

https://forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/api-error-429-help/376113 (2026-08: reports of ~1 h cooldown, ~24 h lock, '60 requests every 6 hours' for GLM-5.2; Kimi K3 429 for 11 h+ then recovered after ~24 h)
https://forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/nvidia-nim-latest-issues/381764 (2026-08-31: K3 'there are days where it works fine and others where you get 429 for an entire day')
https://forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/persistent-nvidia-nim-api-instability-across-multiple-models-429-errors-timeouts-extremely-slow-responses-and-hanging-requests-despite-low-reques/382835
notes: Not a separate wire shape: it is the same 429 body, but lasting from ~1 h to ~24 h on popular or newly released models (GLM-5.1, GLM-5.2, Kimi K3, MiniMax M3). Nothing on the response distinguishes it from a per-minute 429; only the failure of repeated probes does. Reported durations are user guesses (1 h, 6 h, 11 h+, 24 h) from probing at irregular intervals, so they are censored upper bounds, not measured reset times. NVIDIA never confirmed the mechanism (dynamic per-user/per-model limit, capacity guard, or abuse control). Claim by one user that every 429 request resets the timer (bozoweed, 335755 post 6) is unverified and contradicted by a user with built-in escalating backoff who stayed locked for hours (post 7). Decision: still no multiplication on repetition (R10/R13); a lock longer than the 3600 s ceiling is handled by one probe per hour, never a blind bench.

sources: https://forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/nvidia-nim-api-openai-api-error-code-402-cloud-credits-expired-please-contact-nvidia-representatives/316930 (2024-12-16 and 2024-12-24 captures; NVIDIA staff 2025-01-03: 'A fix was recently implemented to resolve this issue')

https://forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/cannot-find-the-amount-of-credits-left-on-nim-api/337051 (NVIDIA staff 2025-06-24: 'we removed the credits system earlier this year')
https://forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/api-credits-for-build-nvidia-com/306633 (staff 2024-09-16: 1000 credits at sign-up, up to 5000)
notes: THE only exhausted-credits shape found, and it is LEGACY: the credit system (1000 credits, up to 5000) was removed in early 2025 per NVIDIA staff, replaced by a per-account request-rate limit shown in the build.nvidia.com UI. No 2026 capture of a 402 was found, so a current key should not normally produce it. It also fired spuriously for users who still had unspent credits (staff acknowledged and 'fixed'), so a lone 402 is weak evidence of a real empty balance. The detail embeds the account id: redact it in any fixture (R43). No distinct 402/403/429 for monthly cap, trial cap or per-model capacity was found: after the credit removal every capacity or abuse limit is the plain 429 (rows 429-*). Rotation can help only if the next key belongs to another account.

sources: https://forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/403-authorization-failed-on-integrate-api-nvidia-com-please-enable-public-api-endpoints-permission-for-my-personal-org/378986 (2026-08-03 capture: HTTP 403 {"status":403,"title":"Forbidden","detail":"Authorization failed"}; key 403s within a minute of creation while /v1/models works)
https://forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/403-authorization-failed-request-to-enable-public-api-endpoints-permission/368546 (2026-04-30)
notes: Reported by many new personal-organisation users: the key lists models (GET /v1/models 200) but every chat call is refused. Users attribute it to a missing 'Public API Endpoints' permission or unfinished account verification (phone/KYC); NVIDIA staff (MarkusHoHo) say account-access issues are not handled on the forum and verification is being worked on. No NVIDIA document states the cause; cause is community inference. Because it is not tied to one model in these reports, scope=credential; but a third-party page says some model families return 403 until the user opens the model page and clicks 'Try API' once (news.creeta.com, uncorroborated), in which case it would be model-scoped, so R24 applies: do not retire the key, 20 s demotion, sibling accounts may work.

sources: https://forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/403-authorization-failed-request-to-enable-public-api-endpoints-permission/368546 (2026-04-30: 'All requests return a 403 status code with no body', models deepseek-v4-pro and glm-5.1)
https://forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/api-problem/375934 (2026-07-07: '403 status code (no body)')
notes: Same situation as the 403 with detail but the body is empty in these reports (possibly client-side stripping; not established). A 403 with an empty body gives no model name, so it cannot be told from the key being dead; per R24 refusing is not proof the key is dead, so no retirement. A different 403 detail ('Invalid UAM response') appeared in a search-engine summary of a forum thread but was NOT verified in a primary post; not recorded as a shape.

message_template: Authentication failed. Please check or regenerate your API key.
rest_rule: auth: 300s, then 3600 after two refuted re-probes
sources: https://forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/title-401-unauthorized-when-calling-nvidia-integrate-api-v1-chat-completions-from-container-api-key-works-for-v1-models-but-fails-for-chat/350380 (2025-11-06: 'HTTP Error 401: Unauthorized / Authentication failed / Please check or regenerate your API key', same key returns 200 on GET /v1/models)
notes: Only one primary capture, and the poster pasted a urllib error line rather than the raw body, so whether the body is JSON {status,title,detail} like 402/403/404 or plain text is NOT established (body=null). The message text is evidenced; the envelope is not. The same key listing models fine but failing chat means a 401 here may be an entitlement problem, not a dead key (see 403 rows), which is why the 300 s auth rule with refuted re-probes (R13) is right instead of retiring. A search summary also mentioned a 401 'Authorization failed' from Hermes Agent; not verified in a primary post.

sources: https://forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/getting-404-error-when-trying-to-use-nim-api-function-not-found-for-account/384928 (2026-10-03 capture: {"status":404,"title":"Not Found","detail":"Function '<uuid>': Not found for account '<id>'"})
https://forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/404-function-not-found-for-account-on-all-chat-completion-requests/377711 (2026-07-22: every model 404 on chat while /v1/models lists them)
notes: An entitlement failure disguised as 404 (R24 treats 404 naming permission/entitlement as denial). Some accounts get it for every model, others for a subset (one search summary: 47 models usable, ~44 not; secondhand); users attribute it to the missing 'Public API Endpoints' permission. Default scope=model (R18); widen to credential only if every model on that key returns it. Account and function ids must be redacted. NOTE: a VS Code client wrapped this same NVIDIA 404 into its own '502 NVIDIA NIM API error: 404 Not Found' (384928 post 1): that 502 is the CLIENT, not NVIDIA; ignore the outer status. Retired models also return 404 (next row).

sources: https://forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/api-error-429-help/376113 (2026-08-15 'error 404 with Kimi' after deprecation; 2026-08-26 'Kimi K3 and DS Flash V4 0731 returning 404 not found now'; model page banner 'This API will be deprecated on 08/24/2026')
notes: A model removed from the hosted catalog stops answering with a 404 while it may still be listed for a while. No body was captured, so it cannot be separated on the wire from the 'Function not found for account' denial; the exact detail text is the only possible discriminator and is not evidenced. If the body says Not found for account, apply the denial row. If a retired model id: no key helps, so surface it (vocabulary request_fault).

sources: https://forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/persistent-nvidia-nim-api-instability-across-multiple-models-429-errors-timeouts-extremely-slow-responses-and-hanging-requests-despite-low-reques/382835 (2026-09-10: 'HTTP 410 errors with GLM-5.2 several times'; another user says 'others will get 410, others will not')
notes: Two user mentions only, tied to GLM-5.2, which carried a deprecation notice for 08/24/2026. No body, no headers. Inference that 410 means 'model gone' is the vocabulary's reading (404/410 on a model id), not an NVIDIA statement. One user ties it to per-user dynamic limits; unproven. If a 410 ever carries a retry number, that would change this row.

message_template: Function id '<function-uuid>': DEGRADED function cannot be invoked
sources: https://forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/status-400-title-bad-request/375165 (2026-07-02 capture for MiniMax-M3; a commenter explains hosted NIM models are NVCF functions with ACTIVE/DEGRADED states and the router rejects instantly; the explanation is the commenter's, not NVIDIA's)
notes: A 400 that is NOT the caller's fault: the function behind the model is marked DEGRADED and the router refuses instantly (no queue). Same problem+json envelope as the 402/403/404 shapes. Key is fine and every key sees it for that model, so rotation multiplies the same refusal: no bench, no retirement; R02 forbids switching model. Vocabulary model_not_ready lists a different model or a later attempt as the fix; the plugin must not treat a 400 as request_fault here, only the 'DEGRADED function' text separates it. Function id redacted.

sources: First-hand by this reviewer 2026-10-16: unauthenticated GET https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1/nonexistent returned 404 text/plain '404 page not found' (Go http.NotFound style)
notes: A wrong path (typo in base URL) is a plain-text gateway 404, not the problem+json envelope. Marked community because it is a single unauthenticated probe, not a documented behaviour. No retry and no rotation help: the URL is wrong. Distinguishable from the entitlement 404 by content-type and by not being JSON.

sources: First-hand by this reviewer 2026-10-16: unauthenticated GET https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1/chat/completions returned 405 with 'allow: POST' and an empty body
notes: Included only to record that the gateway checks method before auth (no 401 on a keyless GET) and returns no body. Not an expected runtime shape for a chat client. The same probe on GET /v1/models returned 200 with only content-type and vary headers: no x-ratelimit-*, no retry-after on a success.
